dissents.topic: Severity of the silent getIamPolicy failure producing PASS

positions.position: P1 — silent failure on getIamPolicy is reported as publicly_shared=False, same label as a verified-private image; either skip or add a tri-state
P1 — complects 'private' and 'unknown' into one boolean; model unknown explicitly
P1 — worst possible failure mode for a security scanner; the test pins the bad behavior
P1 — postcondition is silently weakened; unsafe by default
P1 — false PASS is the worst failure mode for a security scanner
P1 — DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE; emits PASS for what is really 'unknown'

dissents.topic: Whether the Image model should store raw bindings/public_members instead of just a derived boolean

positions.position: P2 — publicly_shared is a derived fact; store bindings as data, derive the boolean at the edge
P2 — Image model is anemic; store the raw bindings/members and roles, decide in the check
P1 — Image ADT is under-specified; missing public_members the PR description promised, needed for actionable remediation
P2 — store the data (public_members), derive the predicate; future checks become trivial
P2 — model lacks tri-state; cannot state invariants from the model alone
Did not flag the model shape as an issue (only flagged loop invariant documentation)

dissents.topic: Whether the bindings scan should consider which role is granted

positions.position: P1 — public-detection logic ignores the role; any role to allAuthenticatedUsers is treated identically, blocking actionable remediation
P2 — does not distinguish viewer-level from owner-level grants; status_extended overclaims
P2 — 'any role to allAuthenticatedUsers counts as public' is the intended semantics, just undocumented; one comment line is enough
P2 — ASYMPTOTICALLY-OK-PRACTICALLY-SLOW; not a blocker but constants will hurt
P2 — complects enumeration and IAM resolution in time; decompose
P2 — frame violation vs. sibling collectors; behavior inconsistent with module convention

issues.description: Silent failure on getIamPolicy is reported as publicly_shared=False, producing a PASS for images whose policy could not be read
issues.detail: In _get_images, when images().getIamPolicy() raises (e.g., 403 Permission denied as exercised by test-image-3, transient API errors, throttling), the except block logs and falls through, appending the Image with publicly_shared=False. The check then emits PASS with status 'is not publicly shared.' Three distinct facts — verified-private, verified-public, unknown — are collapsed into one boolean, which is the worst possible failure mode for a security scanner: false PASS on access denied. Either skip the image, introduce a tri-state (Optional[bool] or an explicit iam_policy_retrieved flag), or emit MANUAL/ERROR rather than PASS. The fixture asserting test-image-3 PASS codifies the unsafe behavior.

issues.description: Naming drift across CHANGELOG, PR description, directory, class, and metadata (compute_image_publicly_shared vs compute_image_not_publicly_shared)
issues.detail: The CHANGELOG entry, directory, file, and class are all 'compute_image_not_publicly_shared', but the PR title and description repeatedly reference 'compute_image_publicly_shared/'. The metadata's CheckID is the negation form while CheckTitle and docstring describe the desired state. The identifier is the contract that flows through tooling, dashboards, and remediation links, so it must be exactly one string everywhere. Pick one convention (positive or negative) and propagate it across CHANGELOG, PR description, metadata, code, and tests.

issues.description: Image model stores only a derived boolean and drops the raw IAM bindings / public_members the PR description promised
issues.detail: The Image BaseModel carries name, id, project_id, publicly_shared. The PR description claims a public_members field, but the model only has the boolean. The service layer interprets the IAM policy before storing it, so the Image value loses the actual fact about the world (the bindings and the offending principals/roles). Downstream remediation cannot tell the operator which members or roles to remove, and future checks (CMEK, deprecated families, role-specific exposure) will need to re-fetch policy. Liskov rates this P1 because the ADT cannot express what a remediator needs; others rate P2 but agree the shape is wrong — store public_members (or raw bindings) and have the check derive the boolean.

issues.description: Public-detection logic ignores which role is granted to allAuthenticatedUsers
issues.detail: The bindings loop sets publicly_shared=True on the first binding whose members contain allAuthenticatedUsers, regardless of role. A binding with roles/compute.imageUser (real exposure) is treated identically to a low-impact role. The model discards which role was granted, so the FAIL status_extended claims 'publicly shared' even when only a low-privilege binding exists, and downstream remediation cannot point the operator at the offending binding. Torvalds rates P1 (model shape + correctness), Dijkstra P2 (status_extended overclaims), Knuth P2 (intended semantics, needs a one-line comment).

issues.description: Loop invariant ('publicly_shared True iff some binding contains allAuthenticatedUsers, any role') is not stated in a literate comment
issues.detail: The inner loop scans iam_policy.get('bindings', []) and sets publicly_shared=True then breaks, ignoring the role attached. The invariant — and the policy decision that any role to allAuthenticatedUsers counts as public — should be one comment line so the next reader doesn't doubt the scope. Also tied to the role-ignoring issue above.

issues.description: Image.id and Image.name accessed with bracket indexing instead of defensive .get; KeyError on missing 'id' would abort enumeration
issues.detail: The code does image['id'] and image['name']. If GCP omits id (deletion in flight, partial response), this raises KeyError, which is swallowed by the outer try and aborts the pagination loop for that project. Use image.get('id', '') / image.get('name') and skip on missing name, and state the invariant: 'every appended Image has a non-empty name; id may be empty string.'

issues.description: _get_images runs serially per project with one synchronous getIamPolicy per image, while sibling collectors use __threading_call__
issues.detail: Sibling enumerations (MIG, disks, etc.) in __init__ use self.__threading_call__(...) to parallelize across regions/zones/projects. _get_images is invoked once, serially, and inside it issues one synchronous getIamPolicy per image per project — O(P*M) sequential round trips. ASYMPTOTICALLY-OK-PRACTICALLY-SLOW. It also complects enumeration and IAM resolution in time. Decompose: collect images, then resolve IAM policies (threaded), then attach. At minimum document why this collector stays serial.

issues.description: images().list(project=...) returns images owned by the project; the 'custom images' scoping is correct but undocumented
issues.detail: The metadata and class docstring say 'custom disk images.' That is correct only because public Google-curated images live in separate projects (debian-cloud, etc.) and are not returned. One literate-comment line stating this invariant prevents a future reader from adding a redundant filter or doubting the scope.

issues.description: test_compute_no_images does not set compute_client.project_ids and does not assert getIamPolicy was not called
issues.detail: The check iterates compute_client.images directly so the test passes — but as a literate-test it should still set project_ids for consistency with sibling tests, and assert that no IAM call was issued on the empty path. A reader of the test file will wonder.

issues.description: Service-level test pins the silent-PASS-on-error semantic as correct (test-image-3 publicly_shared=False on Permission denied)
issues.detail: compute_service_test.py asserts `not compute_client.images[2].publicly_shared` for the image whose getIamPolicy raised 'Permission denied.' This codifies the unsafe contract flagged above and will block the tri-state/skip fix from landing cleanly. Once the unknown-on-error fix lands, this assertion must change to reflect MANUAL/skip/unknown semantics.

issues.description: Check tests round-trip a synthesized boolean instead of driving the full path from IAM bindings to FAIL
issues.detail: The three check tests construct Image(publicly_shared=True/False) directly and assert the check echoes that boolean back. That proves only the trivial `if image.publicly_shared: fail` branch; the IAM-extraction logic and the bindings-to-FAIL seam are never exercised end-to-end through _get_images. TESTED-NOT-PROVED. Add at least one integration-style test that drives a real IAM binding (containing allAuthenticatedUsers) through extraction to a FAIL finding.

issues.description: _get_images is one function doing four interleaved jobs (paginate, fetch IAM, scan bindings, construct Image)
issues.detail: Each of the four steps is a stateless transform over a list. Splitting into _list_images_for_project, _image_iam_policy, and _is_publicly_shared(policy) -> bool would make each piece independently testable and the top-level loop a short comprehension. Right now the bindings scan is buried inside two try blocks and a while loop, which is where future bugs hide.

issues.description: Outer broad `except Exception` around the entire pagination loop hides partial-result semantics
issues.detail: The outer try/except wraps both the list() call and the inner pagination loop. If list_next fails mid-iteration, partial results are silently kept and the rest are dropped; the postcondition 'self.images contains every image in every accessible project' silently weakens to 'some prefix of some images in some projects.' Narrow the except to specific googleapiclient errors, or explicitly document the partial-result contract.

issues.description: error.__traceback__.tb_lineno will raise AttributeError if __traceback__ is None
issues.detail: Both log sites format error.__traceback__.tb_lineno. In re-raised exceptions, mock-injected side_effects, or certain async paths, __traceback__ can be None and the dereference inside the except handler will itself throw an AttributeError, producing a worse failure than the original. The pattern matches existing house style in compute_service.py, so this is a latent footgun being duplicated rather than introduced. Trivial helper (_log_gcp_error) would also shrink call sites.

issues.description: Test asserts type via __class__.__name__ string comparison instead of isinstance
issues.detail: compute_service_test.py uses `assert compute_client.images[0].id.__class__.__name__ == 'str'`. This is isinstance(x, str) written the long way around. Style nit, but it propagates — people copy what's nearby — so worth fixing now while only one site exists.

synthesis.summary: All six reviewers independently land on the same dominant finding: _get_images swallows getIamPolicy failures and emits publicly_shared=False, so an image whose policy could not be read is reported PASS — false-negative-by-construction, the worst failure mode for a security scanner, and the service test currently pins this behavior in place. Five of six also flag that the Image model collapses a tri-state (public / not-public / unknown) and drops the raw bindings or public_members the PR description claims, so remediation cannot tell which principal or role to remove and future checks will have to re-fetch IAM. All six flag the naming drift between the CHANGELOG/directory ('compute_image_not_publicly_shared') and the PR description ('compute_image_publicly_shared') — one identifier should not have two values across artifacts. The strongest preserved disagreement is the severity and framing of the Image-model shape: Liskov treats the missing public_members as P1 (ADT under-specification blocking actionable remediation), while Hickey, Torvalds, Pike, and Dijkstra rate it P2, and Knuth does not flag the model shape at all. A secondary disagreement is whether the role attached to an allAuthenticatedUsers binding should be checked (Torvalds: P1 correctness/model issue; Dijkstra: P2 overclaim in status_extended; Knuth: intended semantics, needs only a one-line comment).
